name: Pork Chops with Apples and Onions
pitch: You've already got the two stars of this dish — the pork and apples do most of the heavy lifting, and a simple pan sauce pulls it all together into something that feels way more special than the effort involved.
steps: Pat your pork chops dry and season both sides generously with salt and pepper. Heat a splash of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat, then sear the chops about 5 minutes per side until nicely browned. Set them aside on a plate.

In the same pan, add a tablespoon of butter if you have it (or just a little more oil). Slice your apples and toss them in — no onion? No problem. A few slices of leek work great, or just skip it and let the apples shine solo. Cook for about 8 minutes until soft and starting to caramelize.
Pour in about a splash (¼ cup) of whatever liquid you have — chicken broth is ideal, but apple juice, beer, or even water will do. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Nestle the pork chops back in, spoon the apple mixture over the top, and cover loosely. Cook on medium-low for another 12–15 minutes until the pork is cooked through and tender.
Serve over rice, mashed potatoes, or just with some bread to soak up that sauce. Spoon plenty of the apple mixture over each chop.

name: Pan-Seared Pork Chops with Apple Pan Sauce
pitch: Pork and apples are a classic pairing, and a quick pan sauce turns two simple ingredients into something that feels really special.
steps: Pat your pork chops dry and season generously on both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat a splash of oil in a skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering, then sear the chops for 3–4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through (internal temp 145°F). Remove and let them rest.
In the same pan over medium heat, add a knob of butter and toss in thinly sliced apple. Cook for 2–3 minutes until softened and lightly golden.
Add a splash of vinegar (apple cider or white wine vinegar works great) and a pinch of garlic, scraping up any browned bits from the pan. Let it bubble for a minute until slightly syrupy.
Spoon the apple pan sauce over your rested pork chops and serve — simple as that!
toolSuggestion: A heavy skillet or cast iron pan for a good sear

name: Soy-Glazed Pork Chops with Roasted Apple Wedges
pitch: A savory-sweet soy glaze gives these pork chops an Asian-inspired twist, and the roasted apples get wonderfully caramelized alongside them in the oven.
steps: Preheat your oven to 425°F. Cut your apples into wedges (no need to peel) and spread them on a baking sheet. Drizzle with oil, season with salt and pepper, and roast for about 10 minutes while you prep the pork.
Whisk together 2 tablespoons soy sauce, 1 tablespoon vinegar, a teaspoon of oil, a pinch of garlic, and a pinch of pepper to make your glaze.
Nestle the pork chops onto the baking sheet alongside the apples and brush them generously with the soy glaze.
Roast everything together for 12–15 minutes, flipping the chops once halfway through and brushing with more glaze, until the pork is cooked through and the apples are tender and caramelized.
Let the chops rest a couple of minutes before serving alongside the sticky, jammy apple wedges.
toolSuggestion: A rimmed baking sheet for even roasting
